"""Test edge cases for the Dataset attribute fix."""

import numpy as np
import xarray as xr
import weldx

def test_backward_compatibility():
    """Test that datasets serialized before the fix can still be loaded."""
    print("=== Testing backward compatibility ===")
    
    # Create a dataset without variable attributes (old style)
    ds = xr.Dataset({
        "var1": (["x"], np.arange(5)),
        "var2": (["x"], np.arange(5, 10))
    })
    ds.attrs = {"global": "attribute"}
    
    print(f"Original dataset attrs: {ds.attrs}")
    for var_name, var in ds.data_vars.items():
        print(f"  {var_name} attrs: {var.attrs}")
    
    # Serialize and deserialize
    ds2 = weldx.asdf.util.write_read_buffer({"ds": ds})["ds"]
    
    print(f"After serialization dataset attrs: {ds2.attrs}")
    for var_name, var in ds2.data_vars.items():
        print(f"  {var_name} attrs: {var.attrs}")
    
    success = ds.identical(ds2)
    print(f"Backward compatibility: {'PASS' if success else 'FAIL'}")
    return success

def test_mixed_attributes():
    """Test dataset with some variables having attributes and others not."""
    print("\n=== Testing mixed attributes ===")
    
    # Create variables with different attribute scenarios
    var1 = xr.DataArray(np.arange(5), name="var1", attrs={"units": "m", "description": "first"})
    var2 = xr.DataArray(np.arange(5, 10), name="var2", attrs={})  # empty attrs
    var3 = xr.DataArray(np.arange(10, 15), name="var3")  # no attrs attribute
    
    ds = xr.Dataset({"var1": var1, "var2": var2, "var3": var3})
    ds.attrs = {"dataset_level": "info"}
    
    print(f"Original:")
    print(f"  Dataset attrs: {ds.attrs}")
    for var_name, var in ds.data_vars.items():
        print(f"  {var_name} attrs: {var.attrs}")
    
    # Serialize and deserialize
    ds2 = weldx.asdf.util.write_read_buffer({"ds": ds})["ds"]
    
    print(f"After serialization:")
    print(f"  Dataset attrs: {ds2.attrs}")
    for var_name, var in ds2.data_vars.items():
        print(f"  {var_name} attrs: {var.attrs}")
    
    # Check preservation
    ds_success = ds.attrs == ds2.attrs
    var_success = all(ds[var].attrs == ds2[var].attrs for var in ds.data_vars)
    success = ds_success and var_success
    
    print(f"Mixed attributes: {'PASS' if success else 'FAIL'}")
    return success

def test_complex_attributes():
    """Test with complex attribute values."""
    print("\n=== Testing complex attributes ===")
    
    complex_attrs = {
        "nested": {"inner": "value", "list": [1, 2, 3]},
        "string": "simple",
        "number": 42,
        "boolean": True,
        "none_value": None
    }
    
    da = xr.DataArray(np.random.rand(3, 3), name="complex_var", attrs=complex_attrs)
    ds = da.to_dataset()
    ds.attrs = {"dataset_info": "complex test"}
    
    print(f"Original complex attrs: {ds.complex_var.attrs}")
    
    # Serialize and deserialize
    ds2 = weldx.asdf.util.write_read_buffer({"ds": ds})["ds"]
    print(f"After serialization complex attrs: {ds2.complex_var.attrs}")
    
    success = ds.complex_var.attrs == ds2.complex_var.attrs
    print(f"Complex attributes: {'PASS' if success else 'FAIL'}")
    return success

def test_coordinate_attributes():
    """Test that coordinate attributes are handled properly."""
    print("\n=== Testing coordinate handling ===")
    
    # Note: This test is mainly to ensure we didn't break coordinate handling
    ds = xr.Dataset({
        "temperature": (["time", "location"], np.random.rand(4, 3)),
    }, coords={
        "time": pd.date_range("2020-01-01", periods=4),
        "location": ["A", "B", "C"]
    })
    
    # Set attributes on the main variable
    ds.temperature.attrs = {"units": "K", "description": "Temperature readings"}
    
    print(f"Variable attrs: {ds.temperature.attrs}")
    
    # Serialize and deserialize
    ds2 = weldx.asdf.util.write_read_buffer({"ds": ds})["ds"]
    print(f"After serialization variable attrs: {ds2.temperature.attrs}")
    
    var_success = ds.temperature.attrs == ds2.temperature.attrs
    coord_success = ds.coords.keys() == ds2.coords.keys()
    
    print(f"Coordinate handling: {'PASS' if (var_success and coord_success) else 'FAIL'}")
    return var_success and coord_success
